subject: MSA / Order Form — proposal for IP indemnity waterfall and defense allocation
messages:
From: Emily Park <epark@halcyonhealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, procurement@halcyonhealth.com
Cc: legal@halcyonhealth.com
Date: Mon, 20 Nov 2028 14:23:00 -0800
Subject: Halcyon MSA comments — IP indemnity scope

Grace — thanks for the call last week. Attached are Halcyon’s redlines to the MSA/order form focused on IP indemnity and third-party claims (file: Halcyon_MSA_comments.pdf). High-level asks from our side: 

- Customer wants comprehensive indemnity for third-party IP claims arising from use of the Service (including allegations tied to model output).
- We expect Redwood to defend and indemnify for such claims, with customer involvement rights; defense control requests are limited — we want the ability to approve counsel if there’s a material conflict.
- Insurance offset: Halcyon is willing to allow Redwood to reduce indemnity by amounts recovered from applicable insurance, but we’d prefer Redwood keep primary responsibility.
- Cap: Halcyon requests a minimum cap tied to a multiple of annual fees (we proposed 5x or $5M floor).

Please confirm a path forward and tell us what Redwood can reasonably accept in first-pass redlines. We’re on a tight procurement timeline — hoping to finalize commercial terms by Dec 8 so we can onboard for the January pilot.

Appreciate quick guidance,
Emily
Emily Park
Director, Legal Operations
Halcyon Health

Attachment: Halcyon_MSA_comments.pdf (pdf)
From: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
To: Emily Park <epark@halcyonhealth.com>
Cc: procurement@halcyonhealth.com, kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 21 Nov 2028 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Halcyon MSA comments — IP indemnity scope

Emily — thanks for the redlines and the timeline. High level: we want to be cooperative but need to preserve protections for model training and customer modifications; we also need a workable operational playbook for notice/evidence so we can respond efficiently.

Initial proposal (attached: Redwood_Proposal_Redline.pdf) — summary of compromises we can accept:

1) Scope: Redwood will indemnify and defend third-party claims that the unmodified Service (the hosted inference API and documented SDKs) infringe a third party’s patent, copyright or trademark to the extent attributable to Redwood’s models or code. Claims arising from customer modifications, customer-provided prompts/content, or customer-hosted models are excluded.

2) Defense control & counsel: Redwood requests primary defense control with the right to appoint counsel. If Halcyon reasonably objects to counsel for a material conflict, Halcyon may propose replacement counsel at its own cost; Redwood will not unreasonably withhold consent. For injunctive relief, we propose to coordinate and allow the customer to retain its own counsel to pursue equitable remedies.

3) Insurance / offsets: Redwood accepts insurance offsets (i.e., amounts actually recovered from a relevant policy reduce Redwood’s indemnity obligation). We propose a mutual cooperation clause for any insurance recovery efforts.

4) Cap & pot: Proposed cap = the greater of (i) $3,000,000 and (ii) total fees paid in the prior 12 months, subject to carveouts for willful misconduct. We’re flagging this as negotiable in line with deal size.

5) Operational: require prompt notice, an evidence checklist (see Evidence_Template.xlsx), and reasonable cooperation. We propose specific SLAs for initial acknowledgement and evidence staging.

Can your team review Redwood_Proposal_Redline and tell us whether Halcyon can accept the defense-control/insurance-offset approach? If not, please flag the specific lines so we can escalate internally. We’re aiming for an agreed redline this week if possible.

Best,
Grace O’Connor
Head of Sales Operations, Redwood Inference
grace@redwood.com | +1 415-555-0123

Attachment: Redwood_Proposal_Redline.pdf (pdf)
From: Halcyon Legal <legal@halcyonhealth.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>
Cc: Emily Park <epark@halcyonhealth.com>, procurement@halcyonhealth.com
Date: Wed, 22 Nov 2028 11:05:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Halcyon MSA comments — IP indemnity scope

Grace — thanks for the quick response and the draft. A few follow-ups from our counsel:

- Defense control: Halcyon cannot accept blanket vendor control for IP claims tied to core product use. For a customer like us, our preference is to lead the defense and control selection; we are open to Redwood appointing primary counsel only where Redwood has compelling operational reasons, but we need the right to participate and to require joint counsel when material defenses affect Halcyon’s broader exposure.

- Cap: Our procurement team will not accept a cap lower than $5M for this tier of commercial use. If Redwood is unwilling to meet the absolute number, we will ask for an alternate structure that provides a carveout for IP claims related to model output (i.e., higher cap for output-related IP claims).

- Insurance offset: Halcyon will accept offset but not to the extent that it reduces Redwood’s indemnity to zero without Redwood first making good-faith contributions. We propose a waterfall: (i) Redwood pays up to the cap, (ii) offsets taken afterwards, or a hybrid that preserves recoverability.

We’ve attached a short counterproposal with redline snippets (Halcyon_Counterproposal.pdf). We’re flexible on language but need to protect our ability to select counsel and secure the cap.

Can your legal team confirm whether Redwood legal can accept either (A) higher cap or (B) a discrete waterfall that prioritizes Redwood liability before insurance offsets?

Regards,
Halcyon Legal

Attachment: Halcyon_Counterproposal.pdf (pdf)
From: kimberly_park <kimberly@redwood.com>
To: grace_oconnor <grace@redwood.com>, ben_carter <ben@redwood.com>, marissa_cole <marissa@redwood.com>
Date: Thu, 23 Nov 2028 08:12:00 -0800
Subject: Internal: proposed waterfall & defense allocation matrix for HS-34271

Team — looping you in with the Halcyon counter. My read: they want customer control or at least a right to select counsel and a $5M floor. Operational asks re evidence and cooperation are standard. I propose we offer a middle path we’ve used before: a short "waterfall + matrix" that maps claim type to control and payment priority. Key bullets below for internal signoff before we respond: 

- Waterfall (payment priority):
  1) Redwood pays indemnity up to $1M (initial liability tranche) without seeking offsets.
  2) If claim > $1M, Redwood and insurance proceeds are applied pro rata up to the cap. Any shortfall after insurance is Redwood’s responsibility up to the agreed cap.
  3) Remaining amounts (above cap) are subject to negotiation / willful misconduct carveout.

- Defense allocation matrix (examples):
  • Patent claims against core hosted API (no customer modification): Redwood may control defense; Halcyon participation rights.
  • Claims tied to model output where customer-provided prompts are central: joint defense or Halcyon-led with Redwood participation.
  • Claims resulting from customer-modified integration or self-hosted components: Halcyon to lead, Redwood to cooperate.

- Counsel selection: allow Halcyon to request replacement counsel if a conflict exists; require mutual good-faith for any replacement decision. For injunctive relief, allow Halcyon to seek equitable remedies and retain counsel.

- Cap: offer to move to $4M floor (compromise) with product/contract playbook that increases to $5M for renewals or upon exceeding usage thresholds.

- Attachments: I’ve populated the Evidence_Template.xlsx with required artifacts and an intake checklist to speed triage.

If everyone agrees, I recommend we present this as Redwood’s internal-legal-approved counter: waterfall + matrix + $4M cap with an escalation to $5M at renewal. If procurement pushes hard for $5M now, Ben — can we model the P&L/insurance risk quickly so we know cost impact?

-K

Kimberly Park
Senior Counsel, Contracts | Redwood Inference
kimberly@redwood.com

Attachment: Evidence_Template.xlsx (xlsx)

Emily — thanks for the counter and Halcyon team for the detail. Per our internal review, Redwood can present the following commercially-final compromise for your team to consider (summarized; see attached redline and evidence checklist):

1) Waterfall & cap: Redwood offers a payment waterfall that preserves a meaningful initial Redwood contribution (first $1M from Redwood), then pro rata treatment with insurance up to an interim cap. We can set the floor cap to $4M now, with a contractual upgrade to $5M tied to either an annual revenue threshold or at first renewal.

2) Defense & counsel: Redwood requests primary defense control for claims clearly tied to Redwood’s hosted service. For claims where customer prompts/content are a material driver, we propose joint defense or Halcyon-led defense with Redwood participation. Halcyon retains the right to request replacement counsel on conflict grounds. For injunctive relief, Halcyon may retain counsel to pursue equitable remedies.

3) Insurance offsets: Redwood accepts insurance offsets but with the waterfall/prioritization above so Redwood’s initial liability is preserved. Both parties will cooperate in insurance recovery and will share recovered amounts per the waterfall.

4) Ops & evidence: use the attached Evidence_Template.xlsx as the single intake artifact — it defines proof (sample prompts, timestamps, system logs, model version, samples, and engineer point-of-contact) and expected SLA for initial acknowledgment (24 hrs) and evidence staging (7 business days).

Next steps:
- Emily / Halcyon — can you confirm whether $4M with a renewal uplift to $5M is acceptable, or whether you require $5M upfront?
- If you accept the waterfall & matrix, we’ll hand the redline to legal for doc prep and loop in procurement to finalize the PO schedule.
- Proposed call: Tue Nov 27 at 10am PT for a 30-minute commercial/legal alignment.

Thanks — happy to jump on a call if useful.

Grace O’Connor
